statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-2100: the p11-kit RPC client can return an uninitialized value, leading to a NULL dereference or undefined behaviour, when C_DeriveKey is called on a remote token with IBM Kyber or IBM BTC-derive mechanism parameters set to NULL (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-2100). The code was added in p11-kit 0.25.6 by https://github.com/p11-glue/p11-kit/commit/aee856f75e06e451a34cb1fdd6630945c9d1623c (CKM_IBM_BTC_DERIVE) and https://github.com/p11-glue/p11-kit/commit/d7523b1031938fdd9740757f90e903aa09f5397d (CKM_IBM_KYBER), and fixed in p11-kit 0.26.2 by https://github.com/p11-glue/p11-kit/commit/39f3b5ed3deccc2772e21ffb7d269329e3ecb600, which reworks p11_rpc_buffer_get_ibm_kyber_mech_param_update() and p11_rpc_buffer_get_ibm_btc_derive_mech_param_update() in p11-kit/rpc-message.c. Debian's tracker names the same introducing and fixing commits and marks its releases with p11-kit older than 0.25.6 as not affected (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-2100). The DHI repository publishes two builds of this owner for Alpine 3.23: 0.25.5-r2 and 0.26.2-r0. 0.26.2-r0 is p11-kit 0.26.2, which contains the fix. 0.25.5-r2 predates the vulnerable code. We checked every ELF file in the p11-kit, p11-kit-server and p11-kit-trust packages of both builds on x86_64 and aarch64 (the -dev, -doc and zsh-completion packages contain no ELF files), each package verified against the repository index checksum. The mechanism and attribute names that the two introducing commits add to p11-kit's constants table ('ibm-btc-derive', 'ibm-kyber', 'ibm-kyber-mode') appear in libp11-kit.so, the p11-kit and trust programs and p11-kit-trust.so of 0.26.2-r0, and appear in no file of 0.25.5-r2, while the older 'ibm-dilithium' entry from the same table is present in both. No published build is affected, so the range ends at the lowest published version, 0.25.5-r2. The scanner matched 0.25.5-r2 only because the CVE record lists every p11-kit version before 0.26.2 as affected.
